idiom_name: closed variant set + ordered structural match with a coverage obligation
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: define one constructor per variant, each carrying only the fields valid in that variant, and write one elimination function per operation whose arms are structural patterns ordered from most specific to most general. The coverage obligation needs an enforcement mechanism that fits the language: a compiler-proved match over a sealed or enum set, a type-level bottom-type check (never / Never / assert_never), or an impossible-case arm that a checker or lint can verify. Keep the wildcard arm for genuinely open input only, and let the compiler - not a comment - be the thing that notices when the variant list grows.
code_sketch:
type Event = Click{x, y} | Key{rune} | Timeout{ms}   # closed set, one arm per variant

handle(e):
    match e:
        case Click(x, y) -> move(x, y)    # a missing arm is a build failure
        case Key(rune)   -> type(rune)
        case Timeout(ms) -> tick(ms)
# no default arm: proving coverage is the compiler's job
pitfalls: Adding a wildcard or else arm converts the coverage proof into a runtime default and hides every variant added later.
Modelling the set as an open hierarchy (subclassable base type, exported enum without a forward-compatibility marker) leaves the compiler unable to prove closure, so it demands an arm that throws.
Patterns test structure, not invariants: a value that matches a shape may still violate domain rules, so validate untrusted input before matching it.

Wrong move: Treat a non-exhaustive Scala match warning or Rust E0004 diagnostic as harmless -> a new variant can become a runtime MatchError or an unhandled branch -> instead promote exhaustiveness diagnostics to errors and enumerate the closed set.

Wrong move: Add a Java default arm merely to silence a sealed-switch diagnostic -> newly permitted subtypes are accepted without an explicit policy -> instead cover each permitted subtype and reserve fallback handling for a deliberate forward-compatibility boundary.
Wrong move: Treat a Python class/sequence pattern as validation -> structurally matching but invalid data enters trusted logic -> instead validate invariants before or inside the matched arm.
